runners_data.name: Big Time Rascal
runners_data.note: Won over this C&D trip in good going recently (1/6f/GOO) and has strong similar-going form (2W3P from 15); as the lone front-runner he has a clear tactical advantage here, though trainer Attwater is 0/8 in the past 14 days and the 5yo carries top weight — the style fit is high and he will be hard to peg back if allowed to control fractions.

runners_data.name: Apple's Angel
runners_data.note: Jim Boyle runner who races as a genuine hold-up type and will sit deepest in the field; similar-going record reads 0W2P from 7 runs and recent form is weak (6,7,8,9), making it hard to see how she converts a rearward position in a 13-runner sprint into a winning effort.

runners_data.name: Barnsnape Boy
runners_data.note: Boyle's second runner, and arguably the more interesting one — won over 7f on good going and has 3W3P from 11 runs on similar ground; his natural style is to come from off the pace but in this race he is squeezed into a midfield berth and will need a strong gallop and a clear passage to land a blow.

runners_data.name: Bated Breeze
runners_data.note: David Egan takes the ride for Gary & Josh Moore (4/31 T14), which is a notable booking; genuine hold-up horse who recorded two thirds on good ground, but the 0W record on similar going and the recent 6th/10th outings suggest he needs the stars to align for a finishing run in a short 6f.

runners_data.name: Coast
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old veteran who wears a blindfold and races from the back; he has a 3rd on good going in his last five but the overall similar-going record is modest (0W1P/15) and he faces the problem all the true closers face today — too many rivals around him and not enough race to run into.|

runners_data.name: Coiled
runners_data.note: Rob Hornby partners this four-year-old who has placed four times on similar going but never won (0W4P/15); the bulk of his form comes over 7-8f rather than 6f, suggesting he may find the trip sharp, and being a true hold-up type in this traffic-heavy field compounds the concern.

runners_data.name: Manhattan Chute
runners_data.note: Longest absentee in the field at 61 days off; all five recent runs have come at 5f at Sandown and Kempton (mostly standard going), so the step up to 6f at Brighton on good-to-firm turf is a significant question mark — the 0W1P similar-going record and 11th last time out make it hard to be confident.

runners_data.name: Mishy's Star
runners_data.note: Wears a blindfold and has a noted tendency to fade in the finish, which is a significant concern in a 6f sprint; her Brighton similar-going record is sparse (2 runs, 0W0P) and recent form over 7-8f suggests she is crying out for a longer trip than today's 6f offers.

runners_data.name: Molly Marine
runners_data.note: Longest lay-off of the main pack at 68 days; trainer Jack Jones is 2/15 in the T14 window and the mare's sole similar-going run produced a 5th — that thin turf record and the rust after a break makes it hard to anchor a forecast on her despite the prominent tendencies she has shown at times.

runners_data.name: Poet
runners_data.note: Carries the warning flag for fading in the finish and the form string (8,9,9,9,7 recent) speaks for itself; Scott Dixon's runner has gone seven starts without placing on similar going (0W0P/15) and the true hold-up style in a sprint field with one front-runner is a very tough ask.

runners_data.name: Port Hedland
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll, who is in excellent form (10/47 T14), sends this five-year-old who won over this exact course and distance on good going (1/6f/GOO) just 7 days ago — the quick turnaround is noted but Carroll does this regularly; Port Hedland is likely to push forward to a prominent position, which is the ideal place to be in today's race shape.

runners_data.name: Some Nightmare
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old who wears a hood and has placed three times in his last six, all on fast ground (Good to Firm or Firm); John O'Shea is in decent form (2/4 T14) and the horse has shown a knack for hitting the board at short trips — he will try to be prominent or at least handy rather than waiting off the pace.

runners_data.name: Valsharah
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's four-year-old (2/25 T14) ran 2nd over 6f on good going in recent form and wears a tongue-tie/blindfold combination; Jason Watson is a quality booking and the horse's similar-going record (0W1P/15) undersells a run that saw it finish second — stepping into the prominent group on today's flat surface gives it a realistic chance.

races.paceDynamic: Big Time Rascal is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner field and, with no genuine pace rival to push him, he can control the tempo from the off on good-to-firm ground at Brighton, dictating fractions that suit a hold-and-quicken approach rather than an all-out burn. The field is dominated by hold-up horses — Barnsnape Boy, Molly Marine, Bated Breeze, Apple's Angel, Coast, Coiled, Mishy's Star and Poet are all genuine come-from-behind types who have been redistributed on the map because the field holds far more hold-up runners than can realistically operate from their natural position; Port Hedland, Valsharah and Some Nightmare are the most likely to push forward and actually secure prominent berths given their recent track records. With one front-runner setting a controlled, uncontested pace and a field stacked with closers who will be crawling over each other at the rear, the race shape strongly favours horses with the tactical speed to sit just off the pace in the top four or five, travel kindly, and land a first run — prominent racers and handy midfield travellers will be best placed, not the true hold-up horses who face a wall of rivals and a short 6f to make up ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Big Time Rascal dictates an uncontested, honest-but-manageable pace and horses tracking him in second or third have the tactical speed to pounce inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Big Time Rascal sets the terms from the front while Port Hedland and Valsharah, both capable of racing prominently, sit within striking range and unleash a late challenge on the rising Brighton finish; with the hold-up pack stuck in traffic, those who positioned handy are rewarded.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Brigade Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If Big Time Rascal sets an unexpectedly strong gallop that strings the field out and creates gaps for closers to exploit in the final 2f.
scenarios.body: A genuine pace creates the runway that the many hold-up types need, allowing Barnsnape Boy or Bated Breeze to pick through a tiring pack; the Brighton uphill finish over 6f can favour late energy if the early splits are fast enough.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Front Pair Coast
scenarios.trigger: If Big Time Rascal slows the race to a crawl and those drawn handy never face a challenge until a sprint-finish kicks off in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: With nothing to press Big Time Rascal, the race turns into a tactical crawl and a sprint from the two-furlong pole; horses with a sharp tactical turn of foot rather than staying stamina win, and prominent types who switched on quickly benefit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Wide Draw Advantages
scenarios.trigger: If the large 13-runner field creates early jostling, several prominent types push forward simultaneously and create a muddling, uneven pace.
scenarios.body: Traffic troubles for the high-drawn hold-up runners lead to a stop-start gallop; a horse with a clean run and tactical versatility — such as Some Nightmare, who has shown consistency from off the pace over shorter — benefits from the ensuing confusion.

watchPoints.text: Port Hedland won over this C&D in good going only 7 days ago under Carroll's in-form yard (10/47 T14) and is likely to push forward prominently — watch whether he can sit on Big Time Rascal's heels and time his challenge to use the Brighton finish.

Big Time Rascal is the lone front-runner and any interference or wide draw at the start could disrupt the controlled pace he needs to set — if he is crowded early, the entire race shape changes and hold-up horses get the strong gallop they require.

Valsharah's combination of Jason Watson, recent 2nd over 6f on good going, and a trainer with live runners (Appleby 2/25 T14) makes him a horse to track from a handy position — if he gets a prominent berth and the pace is honest, he is squarely in the firing line.

The field contains at least eight genuine hold-up horses competing for the same late ground in a 6f sprint; watch the opening furlong to see whether Barnsnape Boy or Bated Breeze push forward against their natural style to avoid being buried in traffic, which would confirm the pace dynamic holds as mapped.

Some Nightmare (John O'Shea 2/4 T14, hood) has placed three of six recently on fast ground and may attempt to race closer than his listed hold-up tag suggests — if he secures a prominent position, his consistency in conditions like today's becomes relevant.

runners_data.name: Parading
runners_data.note: Showed a placing over 7f at Goodwood last time on Good ground which is encouraging for the trip and surface, but is a genuine hold-up horse placed in midfield on the map due to the density of closers in this field — the jockey Finley Marsh will need to find a gap in a six-runner race running off a controlled pace, which limits the upside.

runners_data.name: Radahn
runners_data.note: The one confirmed pace-setter in this field, trained by George Scott who has had three winners from 20 runners over the past fortnight; his OR of 120 and an uncontested lead on Good to Firm ground at Brighton sets up a race entirely to his own terms, and De La Sayette's booking adds further confidence.

runners_data.name: Telegraphic
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with only one run at 7f on Good ground (finished fourth), making this experience relevant; style unknown but the Charlie Johnston yard has been in excellent form at 9/59 over 14 days and this may be a more capable type being underestimated on a single run.

runners_data.name: Better Nature
runners_data.note: Placed third over 7f on Good ground last time, which directly mirrors today's conditions, suggesting the trip and surface are squarely in its favour; Rob Hornby retains the ride and this horse's hold-up profile suits a race where the strong pace-setter does all the work up front.

runners_data.name: Alice Rocks
runners_data.note: Form figures of 5-9 over 6f on Goodwood and Standard surfaces represent modest form, and today's step up to 7f is unproven; a natural hold-up runner that the map places in midfield because of the surplus of closers in this field, meaning its preferred race shape — a truly run affair from the front — is unlikely to materialise.

runners_data.name: Serenity Bay
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in finishes and is 50 days between runs having finished 11th on Good ground over 6f on debut; the step up to 7f may help but the finishing pattern is a concern and Saffie Osborne will need the race to unfold perfectly to get involved.

races.paceDynamic: Radahn is the sole confirmed front-runner in a six-runner field and, with no genuine rival willing or able to press him from the outset, he should be allowed to bowl along at a controlled, self-determined tempo over Brighton's undulating 7f. The going is Good to Firm throughout the card, rewarding horses that travel fluently rather than grind, and Radahn's OR of 120 gives him the class to make that lead count if he can find a rhythm unchallenged. Behind him, the bulk of the field — Parading, Alice Rocks, Better Nature and Serenity Bay — are all natural hold-up types, creating a compressed midfield-to-rear group with little genuine prominent cover between them and the leader. The field holds more hold-up horses than the race map can accommodate at the rear; Parading and Alice Rocks are redistributed to midfield on the map but are true closers, meaning neither is likely to naturally slot into a genuine stalking position — Radahn is far more likely to secure and control the front. This shape strongly favours a horse that can lead at a sustainable gallop and find a gear into the dip, or alternatively a single strong finisher with the class to pick off a potentially untested leader — patient, high-class closers with proven 7f form on similar going are ideally placed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Radahn Leads, Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Radahn bowls along uncontested and sets a measured gallop that suits his own cruising speed
scenarios.body: Radahn dictates from flag to finish on Good to Firm ground at Brighton, controlling the pace through the dip and quickening at the two-furlong pole before rivals can organise a challenge; his OR of 120 and top jockey booking make him the obvious beneficiary of a race run entirely to his own rhythm.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strong Closer Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Radahn's early tempo is deceptively fast and the hold-up horses get a clean run through the dip
scenarios.body: Better Nature or Telegraphic, tracking in midfield on a true Good to Firm surface, find the drop into the Brighton dip triggers their finishing effort at the right moment; with a small field and clear daylight, a well-timed challenge in the final furlong could swamp a front-runner who has given everything early.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Swarm
scenarios.trigger: If Radahn is pushed harder than expected early and ties up inside the final two furlongs
scenarios.body: A faster-than-anticipated early gallop leaves Radahn vulnerable as he climbs the final rise, allowing Better Nature and Telegraphic, who have travelled more economically, to sweep past in the closing stages; this scenario hinges on Radahn's inexperience producing a front-running display that burns his reserves.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Upset From The Rear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is compressed and a true hold-up horse threads a gap late in a slowly-run affair
scenarios.body: Parading or Alice Rocks, both genuine hold-up types despite appearing in midfield on the map, would need a falsely run race and a perfectly timed run through gaps in a small field to get involved; this scenario is marked down because neither horse is truly racing in its natural position and the race shape is unlikely to set up a sustained late burst from deep.

watchPoints.text: Radahn's behaviour at the start is critical — if he misses the break or is taken on early by any prominent mover, the controlled-tempo scenario on which his chance rests dissolves immediately.

Better Nature has directly relevant form (3rd, 7f, Good) and Rob Hornby is a jockey who times his runs precisely — watch where he positions at halfway, as a move to Radahn's girth entering the dip could prove decisive.

Telegraphic is unknown quantity from the Charlie Johnston yard, which is in strong recent form at 9/59; with only one run to judge, this horse could be significantly better than its bare finishing position suggests.

Alice Rocks and Parading are both genuine closers compressed into midfield on the pace map — in a six-runner race with a controlled pace, gaps may not appear late enough for either to land a meaningful blow, and punters should note their natural style is not what the race shape will deliver.

The going is confirmed Good to Firm for this race throughout the card, not the headline Good — horses that showed their best form on softer ground should be treated with caution, while those with proven fast-ground form are enhanced.

runners_data.note: Four wins from five at Brighton over 7f on Good ground makes this a must-respect angle; wears headgear, jockey Darragh Keenan knows the pattern, and five days since last run is a non-issue for a horse in this kind of form — the style-fit flag is irrelevant here as leading is his confirmed role.

runners_data.name: Prefer The Sister
runners_data.note: Trainer James Owen in reasonable form (9/55 over 14 days) and she showed ability with a 7f win on Good last time, but she is a natural hold-up performer squeezed forward on the map because the field has too many closers; on a track where a solo leader controls the tempo, her true come-from-behind style is compromised.

runners_data.name: Kondratiev Wave
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's nine-year-old is fresh off a 39-day break and drops back from 8f to 7f with David Egan taking the ride — two placed efforts at 8f on Firm surfaces suggest he handles quick ground, and tracking an uncontested leader suits his prominent style far better than most in this field.

runners_data.name: Dalmally
runners_data.note: Three consecutive visits to Sandown over a mile on Standard suggest the Brighton 7f on turf is a fresh context; the step back in trip and switch to quicker ground is untested based on recent evidence, and the hold-up style sits poorly against a controlled pace.

runners_data.name: Mighty Ruler
runners_data.note: Seamus Cronin takes a 5lb claim but the horse fell last time out (F in form) and has struggled to fire consistently, with his best recent run a third at 6f on Standard — the step up to 7f on fast turf is speculative and 49 days off adds another variable.

runners_data.name: Romanovich
runners_data.note: William Carson partners a horse with a win at 7f on Good in the recent past and placed efforts on similar ground — he is a genuine hold-up type whose natural position is the rear, though the map shows him in midfield simply because this field cannot accommodate all its closers; the going suits.

runners_data.name: Rainbow Sorbet
runners_data.note: Wears a visor and is by nature a hold-up horse displaced toward midfield on the pace map due to field composition; four runs in total with limited turf experience over 7f, and the step up from 6f is unproven — Jim & Suzi Best have a quiet 14-day record (0/4).

runners_data.name: My Dad Tom
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's three-year-old has been consistently finishing in mid-pack on Good and Standard surfaces, with six placings across 6f-7f suggesting a horse who races honestly but without the sharp finishing gear to capitalise against a well-run front-runner — Pat Dobbs is a quality booking though.

runners_data.name: My Boy Jack
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer whose best recent result was a third at 7f on Good ground, but he has been redistributed to midfield on the map as one of four true closers in a field without room for all of them at the rear; the Kevin & Lauren Frost yard is quiet (0/14 over 14 days) and Mason Paetel's 5lb claim is the main asset.

races.paceDynamic: Dion Baker is the lone confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner field and, with no genuine pace rival to challenge him, he is expected to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset on this flat Brighton seven-furlong trip on Good to Firm ground. Kondratiev Wave is the only other horse with prominent leanings who could push forward, but the field is otherwise stacked with hold-up types — Romanovich, Prefer The Sister, Rainbow Sorbet, and My Boy Jack are all genuine closers who have been redistributed to midfield on the map simply because they cannot all occupy their natural position at the rear in a field this size. With Dion Baker able to dictate an unchallenged tempo and control the fractions, the race shape strongly favours either Dion Baker himself rolling clear uncollected, or a prominent-to-midfield horse who travels close enough to his steady gallop to pounce in the final two furlongs — true hold-up horses finishing from the back against a non-pressured pace are at a material disadvantage here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dion Baker Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Dion Baker leads without any rival applying pressure and the gallop stays controlled throughout the seven furlongs.
scenarios.body: Dion Baker sets his own fractions on the front end, conserves energy through the false flat, and his excellent recent record at this course and distance (four wins from five at Brighton over 7f on Good) allows him to kick again inside the final furlong before rivals can close.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Collects Late
scenarios.trigger: If Kondratiev Wave tracks Dion Baker throughout and times his challenge to overhaul the leader in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Kondratiev Wave has been freshened up (39 days off) and David Egan can place him just off the steady pace, enjoying the slipstream before deploying his finishing effort on fast ground he has handled before; a controlled gallop suits a horse who has placed twice at 8f on firmer surfaces and now drops back to 7f.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses dramatically entering the final two furlongs and the closers find unexpectedly clear ground along the rail.
scenarios.body: Prefer The Sister or Romanovich, despite being mapped ahead of their natural position, are genuine hold-up performers who would benefit if Dion Baker goes too fast early and ties up — Romanovich in particular has a win at 7f on similar Good ground and William Carson is an astute claimer around Brighton.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Bunches, Race Messy
scenarios.trigger: If Kondratiev Wave challenges Dion Baker early and turns the race into a contested lead with pace collapse in the straight.
scenarios.body: A scrambled mid-race creates a bunched finish where horses like My Dad Tom or Mighty Ruler, sitting midfield, may find a cleaner passage than the compressed hold-up group; neither has brilliant recent form but both carry lighter weight and could benefit from chaos.

watchPoints.text: Dion Baker's jockey Darragh Keenan must control the early fractions — if he is allowed to bowl along unchallenged at his own pace, the race could effectively be over turning for home given this horse's Brighton record.

Kondratiev Wave is the only horse with the positional speed to sit on Dion Baker's shoulder; watch at the break whether David Egan commits to tracking him, as that move will define whether this becomes a true test for the leader or a procession.

Romanovich and Prefer The Sister are both natural hold-up performers mapped closer than their true style — if the pace is genuinely slow, neither will have the tactical position to benefit, and punters should watch whether either is forced to make an uncharacteristic move early.

The Going Report confirms Good to Firm for all Brighton races this evening despite the headline "Good" designation — horses with any going concern on fast ground should be monitored, particularly Rainbow Sorbet whose visor headgear and limited fast-ground turf form add uncertainty.

My Boy Jack and Mighty Ruler both arrive with fitness questions (16 and 49 days off respectively) and below-par recent profiles — watch whether either shows early signs of needing the run, which could further compress the chasing pack and benefit Dion Baker's controlled lead.

runners_data.name: Boubyan
runners_data.note: 64 days since last run is the main concern, and Michael Appleby's yard is only 1/24 in the past fortnight suggesting modest current form; a genuine hold-up horse racing in his natural slot, and similar-going form shows one win from six, but the freshness question over 10f on quicker ground needs answering.

runners_data.name: Pershalla
runners_data.note: Amanda Perrett's four-year-old won over 12f on Soft and was placed at 12f on Good, giving her the best distance profile in the field for this step up to 1m2f; though mapped to midfield due to redistribution of the hold-up group, she is a true rear-runner who needs the race run to suit — the [STYLE_FIT] discount applies if the pace is modest.

runners_data.name: Gone Rogue
runners_data.note: Trainer Gary & Josh Moore in good form (2/14 over 14 days) and this five-year-old has a strong recent placed record over 8-10f on Good; a natural hold-up type by profile, he is one of the horses most likely to push forward into a genuine prominent role given how that position opens up with no other prominent runners.

runners_data.name: Super Hit
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on Good ground last time out and has fitness on his side at only 6 days since; the sole front-runner here, his ability to dictate uncontested is the defining tactical factor, though the [STYLE_FIT] tag and step up from shorter trips in recent starts tempers confidence slightly.

runners_data.name: Annexation
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old handicapper who remains competitive at this level, winning at 10f on Good going in his recent history and active at just 7 days since last run; by inclination a hold-up horse, but given the redistribution dynamic, Tony Carroll's runner may find himself pressing forward where he could prove dangerous.

runners_data.name: Voix De Bocelli
runners_data.note: Henrietta Knight's runner has shown little in recent starts (form reads 330897) and none of the last five runs feature a placed finish on Good or Firm ground; a hold-up horse pushed into a compromised mapping position by the field's congestion at the rear, Saffie Osborne's chance depends almost entirely on conditions conspiring in her favour.

races.paceDynamic: Super Hit is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to apply pressure, should stride clear from the gates and control tempo on Good to Firm ground over 1m2f at Brighton. Brighton's undulating track rewards horses that can dictate and avoid trouble, meaning an uncontested lead at a sustainable gallop is a significant tactical asset for Super Hit. The hold-up pack behind — Bownder, Boubyan, Pershalla, Gone Rogue, Annexation and Voix De Bocelli — will be forced to track a single pace-setter, compressing the field and leaving finishers dependent on Super Hit not conserving enough energy to quicken late. This race shape strongly favours a horse that can lead or press from the front, as closers must hope Super Hit ties up or that the pace is honest enough to bring them into play off a long home straight; with a compressed hold-up group and only one true front-runner, that scenario is the exception rather than the rule. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Pershalla, Gone Rogue, Annexation and Voix De Bocelli are all redistributed, and of those, Gone Rogue and Annexation are most likely to push forward and secure prominent positions given their recent form profiles.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Super Hit Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Super Hit breaks cleanly and is allowed to control an uncontested lead throughout at a measured tempo.
scenarios.body: Super Hit sets a comfortable rhythm on Good to Firm ground, conserving energy through the undulations before finding extra in the closing stages when challengers make their move; with no rival willing or able to apply early pressure, the lone front-runner is never headed. Horses with any prominent or pressing inclination — Gone Rogue and Annexation, who may push forward from their redistributed positions — are best placed if Super Hit's advantage is challenged, but the pace-setter's recent win at 10f on Good form underlines the fitness and suitability.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Super Hit sets a genuinely honest pace that stretches the field and leaves enough in the tank for a late closer.
scenarios.body: A sustainable but not dawdling gallop on fast ground allows the freshest finisher to close into the final two furlongs as Super Hit's advantage narrows under pressure; Bownder and Boubyan, natural hold-up horses racing in their correct role, are most likely to produce the sustained finish needed. Boubyan's recent course-form at 8f-10f on Good and Bownder's placed effort at 10f on Good give both a credible profile for this shape, though both need the pace to be genuine enough to bring them into contention.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Challengers Peg Back
scenarios.trigger: If multiple runners push forward early to contest Super Hit's lead, creating a contested pace that tires the front-runner.
scenarios.body: Gone Rogue and Annexation, likely to push forward from their mapped midfield positions given their natural prominent tendencies, could unsettle Super Hit's rhythm and create a faster-run race than anticipated; a contested tempo on this undulating track would open the door for a well-handicapped closer to pick up the pieces. Pershalla, a genuine hold-up type with course-relevant form at 12f on Good (winning on similar going), is the beneficiary if the pace develops honestly and she can be delivered with a late run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — No Clean Shape
scenarios.trigger: If multiple positional battles early cause scrimmaging and the race becomes ragged with no clear beneficiary.
scenarios.body: With several redistributed hold-up types forced into unnatural prominent positions, the early jostling disrupts all pace plans and the race is decided by who avoids trouble rather than tactics; the winner in this scenario is likely to be whichever horse gets the cleanest run through, making form and position largely irrelevant. Voix De Bocelli and Annexation, both racing with compressed preparation windows of 7 days and carrying lower weights, are live dangers in a chaotic shape where class and ratings matter less.

watchPoints.text: Super Hit (J: Christian Howarth 3lb claimer) breaks cleanly — if he does not lead within the first furlong, the entire pace dynamic collapses and hold-up horses become significantly more dangerous.

Gone Rogue and Annexation are both natural hold-up horses likely to push forward early given the gap in the prominent group — watch for early positional jostling in the first two furlongs that could disrupt Super Hit's uncontested lead.

Boubyan returns from 64 days off for a trainer with modest recent strike rate (1/24 in 14 days) — if he shows any signs of ring-rustiness early, he should be discounted from late-challenge scenarios regardless of his Going suitability.

Good to Firm ground is confirmed for this 1m2f trip and favours horses with turf-speed; Pershalla's win came on Soft/Standard, so monitor whether the faster surface blunts her late effort in the straight.

runners_data.name: Outrace
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon runner who hasn't raced in 185 days and whose last five starts produced five last or near-last finishes all on Standard or Soft; the "fades in finish" flag combined with a long absence and entirely different going profile makes this a very hard horse to recommend.|

runners_data.name: Bear Steps
runners_data.note: Unexposed three-year-old for Jack Jones stepping up significantly from 7f to 1m2f for the first time; 11 days since last run, the 10lb claim of the weight allowance helps but trip is unproven, and the trainer is 0/16 in 14 days — interesting if the distance suits but that remains a big if.|

runners_data.name: Mist Of Time
runners_data.note: Three-year-old for William Knight with Saffie Osborne riding, stepping up to 1m2f having shown only one placed run from five on Good ground; the "fades in finish" tag is noted and her form at 7-8f on Standard may not translate cleanly to this faster surface over a longer trip.|

races.paceDynamic: This is an all hold-up field at Brighton over 1m2f on Good to Firm ground, with zero confirmed front-runners meaning the race will almost certainly crawl early before erupting into a sprint finish up the home straight. With every runner in the field carrying a hold-up profile, jockeys will be fighting a tactical vacuum — no one wants to go forward, and the result will be a slowly-run, bunched affair that compresses into a dash over the final two furlongs. The field holds more genuine hold-up types than can all settle naturally at the rear, with Mist Of Time, Dogged, Bear Steps, All About George, Outrace and Launceston all effectively competing for the same rear positions on a track where getting a clear run matters enormously. This race shape heavily favours horses with a sharp turn of foot from a handy position, proven on similar fast ground, and with a jockey capable of threading through a tight-packed group — Myna, Graffiti and Dogged profile best for a sprint-finish scramble.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish Bunched
scenarios.trigger: If the field idles early and the race ignites only in the final 2f, turning a 1m2f contest into a sprint.
scenarios.body: The entire field coalesces into a tight group approaching the home turn, and the winner is whoever finds the cleanest run and quickest gear from midfield; Brighton's uphill finish rewards horses with a sharp, late kick rather than sustained galloping ability.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Myna Dictates Late
scenarios.trigger: If David Egan positions Myna handily off a dawdle and kicks earlier than rivals anticipate.
scenarios.body: Myna's recent Good-ground win over 10f and strong in-form figures give Egan the option to commit for home before the sprint develops; with Tony Carroll's yard firing at 11/50 in 14 days and Myna showing the sole winning profile in this field, an earlier move could steal a march on rivals who leave it too late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Dogged Stays On Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly crawling and the race is run at such a slow tempo that staying ability counts for something up the hill.
scenarios.body: Dogged's three placings at the 10-12f trip on Good ground suggest he handles the conditions and distance better than his form string implies; at age nine he is reliable if the race develops with any meaningful test, and Tony Carroll runs two in this race which adds tactical intrigue.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the muddled pace and messy traffic cause the fancied hold-up runners to block each other and a lightly-regarded runner slips through.
scenarios.body: Bear Steps steps up in trip from 7f and carries the lowest weight as a 3yo; Mist Of Time also has a recent fourth on Good ground at 10f and could benefit if the field fans wide and creates a gap for a runner improving into the distance.

watchPoints.text: Watch Myna for an early move from David Egan — in a field of hold-up horses with no genuine pace, a jockey of Egan's quality could commit Myna for home off the final bend before rivals react, and with the best recent form in the field this is the most likely race-changing manoeuvre.

Watch for a significant traffic problem in the straight — with eight hold-up horses all tracking each other into the home turn on Brighton's narrow track, at least two or three runners will find themselves blocked or forced wide, and Launceston and All About George are most vulnerable given their wide draws and form concerns.

Bear Steps is worth monitoring on the way to the start — stepping up 5f in trip for the first time and the trainer at 0/16 in 14 days, any signs of greenness or reluctance in the preliminaries would be a red flag for an already speculative runner.

Dogged and Myna are both Tony Carroll runners — watch for any jockey instructions that hint at which horse Carroll considers his first string, as Dogged could be asked to set a token pace to soften the race up for the stablemate.

Check the going report carefully — the 7:50 race earlier on the card is already logged as Good to Firm for the 1m2f trip, meaning the ground will likely ride faster still by the 8:20, which will amplify the sprint-finish nature of the race and favour the horse with the sharpest acceleration.

runners_data.name: Rory Rocket
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on good ground 28 days ago with Jude Fernandes (7lb claimer reducing weight burden) and has multiple wins in the form string — the hold-up style will rely on Kento's pace being sufficient, but recent course-and-distance confidence makes this the most credible closing threat.

runners_data.name: Too Darn Good
runners_data.note: Henry Candy's three-year-old has a placed effort at 5f on good going but has failed to win in nine similar-going runs and the form string shows a consistent inability to convert; the hood (headgear) may sharpen focus, but Rob Hornby will need things to fall right from midfield.

runners_data.name: Kento
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's five-year-old set to lead as the race's only confirmed front-runner on ground he handles, with four placed efforts from 15 similar-going starts suggesting competitiveness rather than dominance; raced eight days ago, so freshness is adequate, but the style-fit flag is a mild caution — Carroll's runner is most effective when pressing rather than fully dominating.

runners_data.name: Faustus
runners_data.note: Rachel Cook & John Bridger's eight-year-old brings solid experience at 5f on good ground — including a second place from 15 runs on similar going — but is a genuine hold-up horse whose true position will be further back than the map shows; Ryan Kavanagh's 3lb claim helps at the weights, yet the style displacement means a late run depends heavily on Kento burning them off.

runners_data.name: Honour Your Dreams
runners_data.note: Michael Attwater's six-year-old has posted two seconds from 15 runs on similar going and is consistent enough to place, but the headgear switch to a tongue-tie flags a trainer seeking more; Alistair Rawlinson will need to find a position closer to the pace than this horse naturally settles, as genuine hold-up tactics from the back against a controlled front-runner over 5½f at Brighton represent a tough ask.

races.paceDynamic: Kento is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-runner sprint over Brighton's 5½f, and with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, David Egan can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front. The remaining four runners — Rory Rocket, Too Darn Good, Faustus, and Honour Your Dreams — are all hold-up or prominent types, meaning the tempo Kento sets will be measured rather than searching, reducing the premium on stamina and increasing the value of positional speed off the pace. Faustus and Honour Your Dreams are genuine hold-up horses pushed into the midfield map position by redistribution; neither is likely to travel quite as close to the pace as their mapped slot implies, meaning the field will string out behind Kento with the closers needing a meaningful late surge on good-to-firm ground. This race shape strongly favours a well-positioned stalker or a horse with the tactical speed to sit just off Kento's shoulder and pounce in the final furlong, rather than a true deep closer relying on a strong pace to run into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kento Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Kento leads as expected and Egan controls the tempo, denying rivals a strong enough gallop to close.
scenarios.body: Kento sets a comfortable pace from the front on good-to-firm ground and, having made every yard, finds enough to hold on as the closers' late runs fall marginally short; this scenario rewards the horse already in the ideal position with no tactical disruption.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Stalker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent-tracking runner sits just off Kento through the bend and delivers a sustained late challenge inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Rory Rocket, who showed a win at 6f on good ground in recent form, could sit in Kento's slipstream and outstay him on the run-in; this suits a horse with genuine racecourse form over similar trips and conditions rather than the redistributed hold-up types further back.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Kento's controlled pace is genuinely slow enough to compress the field and allow the deepest closers to reel the leader in during the final 100 yards.
scenarios.body: Faustus or Honour Your Dreams would need the pace to collapse in the closing stages to make up the ground from their true rearward starting positions; given both are racing somewhat out of their natural hold-up role and the pace is unlikely to be truly extreme, this scenario carries limited probability.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Break Scrambles Race
scenarios.trigger: If there is a slow break or significant positional disruption at the start that negates Kento's expected clean lead.
scenarios.body: A chaotic start could compress the field immediately and turn the race into a sprint from the off, favouring a horse with raw finishing speed regardless of style; Too Darn Good, with a third-place finish on similar good ground over 5f in recent form, retains some tactical flexibility in a scrambled race.

watchPoints.text: Kento — if David Egan is allowed a clean, unchallenged lead through the early furlongs, the winning probability increases sharply; watch for whether any rival applies pressure into the first two furlongs, as that is the critical variable.

Rory Rocket — Jude Fernandes' 7lb claim makes this hold-up runner potentially well-weighted at OR 65; watch whether Fernandes can position closer than expected given the small field, as that changes its scenario from C-type closer to B-type stalker.

Faustus and Honour Your Dreams — both are true hold-up horses running in a race that will not generate the strong gallop they need; if either visibly fails to travel or is off the bridle earlier than expected, that is the redistribution effect playing out in real time.

Going confirmation — the course report lists this race as Good to Firm throughout the card despite the official Good designation; horses with a Going=OK flag have been assessed as handling this, but monitor any drying-out trend as the evening card progresses that could firm the surface further.
